newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK, S'pore investors prop up East London property.
newsitem.headline: HK, S'pore investors prop up East London property.

text.p: Investors from Hong Kong and Singapore have helped swell sales of residential units in the Docklands region in East London, the London Docklands Development Corp (LDDC) said on Friday.

"We are witnessing a return to the high level of property sales activity of the 1980s, but with a broader base of purchasers, including a substantial number from Hong Kong and Singapore," Michael Pickard, LDDC chairman, said in a statement.
LDDC is reponsible for encouraging more projects and development in the East London area.
Over 850 homes were sold in London Docklands in the first half of 1996, similar to the number sold for the whole of 1995. Asian investments in Docklands housing account for 20 percent, the statement.
Pickard, currently in Hong Kong to market Docklands residential properties, said the area has attracted over 6.3 billion stg in private investments, but did not specify the period.
The area now houses 2,400 businesses and has a residential population of more than 72,000.
